generated_examples.rule: Each source row becomes one research-only example with the same official URL, fact, gate and confidence. No parcel policy relation, grey-belt status, mineral safeguarding status, site allocation, permission or Future Growth score is inferred.

second_pass_examples.rule: Each source row is rendered a second time as a fail-closed control. Dataset, plan, boundary, category or geography presence remains separate from exact current parcel-level legal/policy effect.

extra_examples.ref: Green Belt annual snapshot freshness gate
extra_examples.fact: Planning Data says Green Belt annual returns are a snapshot and may not reflect changes made after authorities submitted them.
extra_examples.gate: Re-read the current adopted authority policy map before using a national snapshot intersection.

extra_examples.ref: Green Belt versus grey belt separation
extra_examples.fact: Current guidance treats grey-belt assessment as a separate policy test within Green Belt decision making.
extra_examples.gate: Do not label a parcel grey belt solely because it lies inside Green Belt geometry.

extra_examples.fact: NPPF allows Green Belt boundaries to be altered through plan preparation where the policy tests are met.
extra_examples.gate: Release through a plan is not itself planning permission for development.

extra_examples.fact: NPPF states safeguarded land is not allocated for development at the present time and permanent development should follow a plan update proposing it.
extra_examples.gate: Do not score safeguarded land as an adopted development allocation.

extra_examples.fact: The Planning Data mineral-safeguarding-area dataset currently has zero providers and no collection attempt.
extra_examples.gate: No platform hit cannot be interpreted as no mineral safeguarding constraint.

extra_examples.fact: Government minerals guidance distinguishes safeguarding from permission to extract and notes other permits and approvals can also be required.
extra_examples.gate: A safeguarded resource is neither a guaranteed extraction site nor an automatic prohibition on non-mineral development.

extra_examples.fact: Waste-plan boundaries identify the geography covered by a waste plan.
extra_examples.gate: Boundary intersection does not identify a waste facility, allocation or consent.

extra_examples.fact: The local-plan-boundary dataset is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
extra_examples.gate: Use it for plan routing only until current authority plan status and boundary are confirmed.

extra_examples.fact: The emerging-plan record explicitly says it is a placeholder to help the authority provide data.
extra_examples.gate: Do not convert the placeholder into an assumed plan stage, timetable or policy status.

extra_examples.fact: The record is marked adopted but its recorded plan period ended 1 January 2018.
extra_examples.gate: An old adopted label cannot override the need to identify the current development plan.

extra_examples.fact: The record's plan period ended 1 January 2026, before the current July 2026 research date.
extra_examples.gate: Treat the record as historical/contextual until the current authority development-plan position is verified.

extra_examples.ref: Darlington adopted plan not parcel allocation
extra_examples.fact: The Darlington record is adopted and includes an area-wide required housing figure.
extra_examples.gate: Adoption and housing requirement do not identify a target parcel as allocated or permissioned.

extra_examples.fact: The Merton plan record includes an authority-wide required-housing figure.
extra_examples.gate: Do not divide or transfer the area requirement into parcel capacity without the actual allocation and site evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data currently reports only five supplementary plans from two providers.
extra_examples.gate: Absence from the national dataset is not evidence that an authority has no applicable supplementary plan or guidance.

extra_examples.fact: The plan-event dataset provides categories such as adoption and consultation milestones.
extra_examples.gate: A category record is not proof that a named plan has reached that milestone.

extra_examples.fact: Cambridge is an authoritative Green Belt core category.
extra_examples.gate: The category contains no parcel geometry; use the actual Green Belt geography layer for intersection.

extra_examples.fact: York's Green Belt entity provides authoritative downloadable geometry.
extra_examples.gate: Only an exact canonical parcel intersection can establish geometric overlap; policy consequences still require the current plan.

extra_examples.ref: Minerals and waste plan provenance gate
extra_examples.fact: The Herefordshire minerals/waste record is quality 'some' and links the authority plan.
extra_examples.gate: Use the authority's current plan and policy maps before assigning any parcel constraint.

extra_examples.fact: The authoritative joint waste-plan boundary spans multiple boroughs and a development corporation.
extra_examples.gate: A cross-boundary plan geography must not be confused with a site allocation or facility catchment.

extra_examples.ref: Green Belt Golden Rules consent separation
extra_examples.fact: NPPF Golden Rules specify contributions for qualifying major housing development on released or certain Green Belt land.
extra_examples.gate: Compliance can carry planning weight but does not itself grant planning permission or prove a site qualifies.
